newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish president to sign 1997 budget today.
newsitem.headline: Polish president to sign 1997 budget today.

text.p: Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski will sign the 1997 national budget on Monday, his press office said.
It said in a statement that the signing ceremony was scheduled for 1500 GMT.
On Friday, the lower house of parliament gave a final go ahead to the budget draft after rejecting the Senate's proposals to boost spending on agriculture.
The bill, seen as the continuation of the three previous budgets of the ruling leftist coalition, envisages this year's deficit at 2.8 percent of GDP.
It assumes that inflation will be cut to 13 percent year-on-year in December 1997 from last year's 18.5 percent while the gross domestic product will grow by 5.5 percent.
It provides for a slight real-term increase in spending for most underfinanced areas such as education, health care, law enforcement and justice system and defence.
